title: Adaptation of Bayesian decision analysis for clinical trial design to binary outcomes: illustration for Ebola virus disease treatment.
abstract: When designing trials for high-mortality diseases with limited therapies, the conventional 5% type I error rate (α) may be unsuitable. A higher α could benefit seriously ill patients lacking therapeutic alternatives. Bayesian decision analysis (BDA) integrates multiple health consequences into trial design. We extend BDA for trials with binary outcomes to calculate optimal sample sizes (n) and α in an Ebola outbreak context. We consider fixed, two-arm randomized trials with binary outcomes and two types of clinical trial losses: post-trial loss, for not approving an effective treatment or approving an ineffective one; in-trial loss, for not administrating an effective treatment to control-arm patients or for administrating an ineffective treatment to experimental-arm patients. The model incorporates treatment side effects and disease severity into a single loss function, from which BDA-optimal n and α are derived. Using mortality as the outcome, we modeled various epidemic scenarios by varying target population size, mortality rate, and treatment efficacy. In most cases, BDA-optimal α exceeded the conventional one-sided 2.5% and sample sizes are smaller. Simulations comparing BDA-optimized two-arm trials (fixed/sequential) to conventional designs (two-arm/single-arm, fixed/sequential) across outbreak scenarios show comparable statistical power across designs, except when sample size assumptions are incorrect, or when trials started after the outbreak peak; in these situations, BDA-optimized trials show superior powers. This BDA framework provides a promising approach for designing trials with binary outcomes, particularly in high-mortality disease outbreaks, where declining case numbers and uncertain mortality and efficacy data challenge conventional methods.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 当设计治疗方法有限的高 死亡率 疾病的试验时,传统的 5% I 型错误率 (α) 可能不合适。较高的α可能有益于缺乏治疗替代方案的重病患者。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们考虑具有二元结果和两种类型的临床试验损失的固定双组随机试验:试验后损失,因为不批准有效的 治疗 或批准无效的 治疗;试验中失败,因为未对对照组患者施用有效的 治疗 或对实验组患者施用无效的 治疗。
elements_zh.methods: 贝叶斯决策分析 (BDA) 将多种健康后果整合到试验设计中。使用 死亡率 作为结果,我们通过不同的目标人群规模、死亡率 发生率和 治疗 功效来模拟各种流行病场景。
elements_zh.main_results: 在大多数情况下,BDA 最优 α 超过了传统的单侧 2.5%,并且样本量较小。在 暴发 场景中将 BDA 优化的双臂试验(固定/序贯)与传统设计(双臂/单臂、固定/序贯)进行比较的模拟显示,不同设计的统计功效具有可比性,除非样本量假设不正确,或者试验在 暴发 峰值之后开始;在这些情况下,BDA 优化的试验显示出卓越的功效。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该模型将 治疗 副作用和疾病严重程度纳入单个损失函数,从中导出 BDA 最佳 n 和 α。该 BDA 框架为设计具有二元结果的试验提供了一种有前途的方法,特别是在高 死亡率 疾病 暴发 中,其中病例数下降和不确定的 死亡率 和疗效数据对传统方法提出了挑战。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究结果提供了一种根据多种健康后果优化样本量和 I 型错误率的方法,为高 死亡率 疾病(特别是 埃博拉病毒病)的临床试验设计提供了谨慎的信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该模型假设固定的双臂随机试验,并且没有考虑所有可能的临床试验损失。由于模型的假设和限制,证据强度中等。

title: Early detection of immunoglobulin A against a vaccine backbone protein enables fast, durable, and objective identification of individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus.
abstract: BACKGROUND: rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccine is recommended for prevention of Ebola virus (EBOV) infection and disease (EVD). However, breakthrough EBOV infections have been observed in vaccinees. Currently available diagnostic and research assays cannot reliably distinguish individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus from those previously infected with the virus. This limitation complicates interpretation of vaccine-effectiveness studies, seroepidemiologic investigations, and estimates of infection or attack rates. The ability to differentiate vaccine-induced immune responses from those resulting from natural infection remains an important unmet public health and research need. METHODS: We developed a multiplex sero-diagnostic assay simultaneously detecting IgA, IgG, and IgM antibodies against vesicular stomatitis Indiana virus nucleoprotein (VSV-N), a vaccine-specific marker absent in natural infection, and EBOV-GP, the vaccine's target antigen. We evaluated longitudinal samples from 30 individuals after vaccination and 30 placebo (saline) recipients, as well as 8 participants from a long-term vaccination follow-up study. FINDINGS: We detected increase in all antibodies against both protein antigens in vaccinated individuals. Critically, the assay reveals that anti-VSV-N IgA responses emerge earlier and more robustly than anti-GP responses in vaccinees, establishing anti-N IgA as a definitive, early, and durable biomarker of rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccination with high sensitivity and specificity. INTERPRETATION: The assay enables rapid, accurate identification of vaccine recipients and supports real-time assessment of vaccine effectiveness during outbreaks. Furthermore, the assay's adaptability to the expanding pipeline of VSV-vectored vaccines positions it as a transformative diagnostic platform for accelerating preparedness for future infectious disease threats and outbreak response strategies. FUNDING: Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The National Cancer Institute (NCI) and the Divisions of Intramural Research (DIR) and Clinical Research (DCR) of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) at the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH).

title_zh: 针对 疫苗 骨架蛋白的免疫球蛋白 A 的早期检测能够快速、持久和客观地识别接种 埃博拉病毒 疫苗的个体。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccine is recommended for prevention of Ebola virus (EBOV) infection and disease (EVD). However, breakthrough EBOV infections have been observed in vaccinees. This limitation complicates interpretation of vaccine-effectiveness studies, seroepidemiologic investigations, and estimates of infection or attack rates. METHODS: We developed a multiplex sero-diagnostic assay simultaneously detecting IgA, IgG, and IgM antibodies against vesicular stomatitis Indiana virus nucleoprotein (VSV-N), a vaccine-specific marker absent in natural infection, and EBOV-GP, the vaccine's target antigen. We evaluated longitudinal samples from 30 individuals after vaccination and 30 placebo (saline) recipients, as well as 8 participants from a long-term vaccination follow-up study. Critically, the assay reveals that anti-VSV-N IgA responses emerge earlier and more robustly than anti-GP responses in vaccinees, establishing anti-N IgA as a definitive, early, and durable biomarker of rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccination with high sensitivity and specificity. INTERPRETATION: The assay enables rapid, accurate identification of vaccine recipients and supports real-time assessment of vaccine effectiveness during outbreaks. Furthermore, the assay's adaptability to the expanding pipeline of VSV-vectored vaccines positions it as a transformative diagnostic platform for accelerating preparedness for future infectious disease threats and outbreak response strategies. title: The Storm We Chose: Bundibugyo Virus, Preparedness Injustice, and the Pathogens We Decline to Fight.
abstract: ABSTRACT The 2026 Ebola disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda is caused by Bundibugyo virus, a species for which, unlike Zaire ebolavirus , no licensed vaccine and no approved therapeutic exist. This commentary argues that this absence is not a misfortune of virology but a structurally produced injustice. Bundibugyo virus has been characterised since 2008, has caused lethal outbreaks, and was foreseeably capable of recurrence; more importantly, species‐specific and cross‐protective countermeasures were scientifically tractable more than a decade before, yet none reached licensure or field readiness. A recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus vaccine expressing the Bundibugyo glycoprotein — built on the same platform as the licensed Zaire vaccine — conferred complete protection in nonhuman primates in 2013; thirteen years later, no clinical‐grade material existed when the outbreak began. The gap, we argue, lay not in what science could build but in what the system chose to finish, because preparedness investment concentrated on the species that threatened wealthier and more connected populations. title_zh: 我们选择的风暴:本迪布焦病毒、准备不公以及我们拒绝对抗的病原体。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT The 2026 Ebola disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda is caused by Bundibugyo virus, a species for which, unlike Zaire ebolavirus , no licensed vaccine and no approved therapeutic exist. This commentary argues that this absence is not a misfortune of virology but a structurally produced injustice. Bundibugyo virus has been characterised since 2008, has caused lethal outbreaks, and was foreseeably capable of recurrence; more importantly, species‐specific and cross‐protective countermeasures were scientifically tractable more than a decade before, yet none reached licensure or field readiness. A recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus vaccine expressing the Bundibugyo glycoprotein — built on the same platform as the licensed Zaire vaccine — conferred complete protection in nonhuman primates in 2013; thirteen years later, no clinical‐grade material existed when the outbreak began. The gap, we argue, lay not in what science could build but in what the system chose to finish, because preparedness investment concentrated on the species that threatened wealthier and more connected populations. Drawing on the framework of structural injustice and on the authors’ prior field experience of concurrent epidemics in the DRC, we distinguish tragic scarcity from produced scarcity, answer the feasibility objection, and argue that closing the gap is an obligation rather than a charity.

title: Cross-border preparedness, health worker protection, and institutional response in the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak
abstract: This Perspective presents the author’s own analytical position on the international response to the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, rather than a systematic assessment of the evidence. On 17 May 2026, WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), the second-highest alert level under the International Health Regulations (IHR) as amended in 2024. Three interlinked themes are examined: cross-border preparedness under the amended IHR and the WHO Pandemic Agreement (adopted 2025, not yet in force); frontline health worker protection, illustrated by four healthcare-worker deaths within four days of the initial alert; and institutional response and research investment, illustrated by the continued absence of a licensed, Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or therapeutic and by disparities in access to advanced care. Genuine early action has coexisted with weak cross-border screening coordination, gaps in healthcare worker protection, and limited community engagement, illustrated by the burning of an Ebola treatment centre in Rwampara; these gaps appear, on the evidence available, to reflect governance weaknesses, financing shortfalls, and insecurity rather than any single cause. The Perspective closes with recommendations on cross-border surveillance protocols, healthcare worker protection, community engagement, and equitable neglected-pathogen research investment, for policymakers, Africa CDC, WHO, and practitioners.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the international response to the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, examining cross-border preparedness under the amended IHR and WHO Pandemic Agreement, frontline health worker protection, and institutional response and research investment. The central question is how these factors influenced the management of the outbreak and what lessons can be drawn for future preparedness.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a Perspective rather than a systematic assessment of the evidence. It does not report on databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study counts. The author presents an analytical position on the international response to the BVD outbreak, without conducting a meta-analysis or consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that genuine early action coexisted with significant weaknesses in cross-border screening coordination, healthcare worker protection, and community engagement. It concludes that these gaps reflect governance weaknesses, financing shortfalls, and insecurity rather than any single cause. The absence of a licensed, Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or therapeutic is noted as a critical institutional response issue.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies gaps in healthcare worker protection and cross-border coordination as key controversies. It also notes the limited community engagement, exemplified by the burning of an Ebola treatment centre in Rwampara, which suggests unresolved challenges in public health communication and trust-building. The evidence does not provide a comprehensive analysis of these issues, leaving them as unresolved gaps.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends cross-border surveillance protocols, improved healthcare worker protection, enhanced community engagement, and equitable research investment in neglected pathogens. These recommendations are directed at policymakers, Africa CDC, WHO, and practitioners to strengthen future responses to similar outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This review analyzes the international response to the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda. It highlights cross-border preparedness under the amended IHR and WHO Pandemic Agreement, frontline health worker protection, and institutional response challenges. The review notes the absence of a licensed vaccine or therapy for BVD and the burning of an Ebola treatment centre in Rwampara as examples of governance and community engagement failures. It concludes that these gaps reflect systemic issues rather than isolated causes. The review recommends improved surveillance, healthcare worker safety, community engagement, and equitable research investment to address these challenges and enhance future outbreak responses.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the international response to the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, examining cross-border preparedness under the amended IHR and WHO Pandemic Agreement, frontline health worker protection, and institutional response and research investment. The central question is how these factors influenced the management of the outbreak and what lessons can be drawn for future preparedness.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a Perspective rather than a systematic assessment of the evidence. It does not report on databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study counts. The author presents an analytical position on the international response to the BVD outbreak, without conducting a meta-analysis or consensus process.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that genuine early action coexisted with significant weaknesses in cross-border screening coordination, healthcare worker protection, and community engagement. It concludes that these gaps reflect governance weaknesses, financing shortfalls, and insecurity rather than any single cause. The absence of a licensed, Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or therapeutic is noted as a critical institutional response issue.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies gaps in healthcare worker protection and cross-border coordination as key controversies. It also notes the limited community engagement, exemplified by the burning of an Ebola treatment centre in Rwampara, which suggests unresolved challenges in public health communication and trust-building. The evidence does not provide a comprehensive analysis of these issues, leaving them as unresolved gaps.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends cross-border surveillance protocols, improved healthcare worker protection, enhanced community engagement, and equitable research investment in neglected pathogens. These recommendations are directed at policymakers, Africa CDC, WHO, and practitioners to strengthen future responses to similar outbreaks.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于2026年发生在刚果民主共和国(DRC)和乌干达的邦迪布古病毒疾病(BVD)暴发的国际应对措施,探讨修订后的IHR和WHO大流行协议下的跨境准备、一线医护人员保护以及机构应对和研究投资。核心问题是这些因素如何影响暴发的管理,以及未来准备可以从中吸取哪些教训。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是一篇观点文章,而非对证据的系统评估。它未报告数据库、检索日期、纳入标准或研究数量。作者以个人分析的角度呈现了对BVD 暴发国际应对措施的看法,未进行元分析或达成共识的过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述指出,真正的早期行动与跨境筛查协调不足、医护人员保护存在漏洞以及社区参与有限并存。它得出结论,这些差距反映了治理薄弱、资金不足和安全问题,而非单一原因。尚未有针对邦迪布古病毒的获批疫苗或治疗药物被指出为机构应对中的关键问题。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,医护人员保护和跨境协调的不足是主要争议点。它还提到社区参与有限,例如在鲁万帕拉(Rwampara)发生了一家埃博拉治疗中心被焚毁的事件,这表明在公共卫生沟通和信任建立方面仍存在未解决的挑战。现有证据并未对这些问题进行全面分析,因此它们仍被视为未解决的差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述建议制定跨境监测协议、改善医护人员保护、加强社区参与,并在被忽视病原体上实现公平的研究投资。这些建议旨在为政策制定者、非洲疾病预防控制中心(Africa CDC)、世界卫生组织(WHO)和实践者提供参考,以增强未来对类似暴发的应对能力。

title_zh: 跨境准备、医护人员保护和机构应对在2026年邦迪布古病毒疾病暴发中的作用
source_body_en: This Perspective presents the author’s own analytical position on the international response to the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, rather than a systematic assessment of the evidence. On 17 May 2026, WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), the second-highest alert level under the International Health Regulations (IHR) as amended in 2024. Three interlinked themes are examined: cross-border preparedness under the amended IHR and the WHO Pandemic Agreement (adopted 2025, not yet in force); frontline health worker protection, illustrated by four healthcare-worker deaths within four days of the initial alert; and institutional response and research investment, illustrated by the continued absence of a licensed, Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or therapeutic and by disparities in access to advanced care. Genuine early action has coexisted with weak cross-border screening coordination, gaps in healthcare worker protection, and limited community engagement, illustrated by the burning of an Ebola treatment centre in Rwampara; these gaps appear, on the evidence available, to reflect governance weaknesses, financing shortfalls, and insecurity rather than any single cause. The Perspective closes with recommendations on cross-border surveillance protocols, healthcare worker protection, community engagement, and equitable neglected-pathogen research investment, for policymakers, Africa CDC, WHO, and practitioners.
abstract_zh: 本文以作者个人的分析观点呈现,而非对证据的系统评估,聚焦于2026年发生在刚果民主共和国(DRC)和乌干达的邦迪布古病毒疾病(BVD)暴发的国际应对措施。2026年5月17日,世界卫生组织(WHO)宣布暴发为国际关注的突发公共卫生事件(PHEIC),这是根据2024年修订的《国际卫生条例》(IHR)所设定的第二高警戒级别。本文探讨了三个相互关联的主题:根据修订后的IHR和WHO大流行协议(2025年通过,尚未生效)下的跨境准备;一线医护人员保护,这体现在初始警报发布后四天内有四名医护人员死亡;以及机构应对和研究投资,这体现在尚未有针对邦迪布古病毒的获批疫苗或治疗药物,以及先进护理获取的不平等。真正的早期行动与跨境筛查协调不足、医护人员保护存在漏洞以及社区参与有限并存,例如在卢旺达的鲁万帕拉(Rwampara)发生了一家埃博拉治疗中心被焚毁的事件;这些差距似乎反映了治理薄弱、资金不足和安全问题,而非单一原因。本文最后为政策制定者、非洲疾病预防控制中心(Africa CDC)、世界卫生组织(WHO)和实践者提出了关于跨境监测协议、医护人员保护、社区参与以及对被忽视病原体的公平研究投资的建议。

title: Longitudinal Filovirus Seroreactivity Following Ad26.ZEBOV (Zabdeno) and MVA-BN-Filo (Mvabea) Vaccination in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
abstract: Background: Filoviruses, specifically Ebola virus (EBOV), Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), and Marburg virus (MARV), have been the etiologic agents of multiple outbreaks of severe disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Two EBOV-specific vaccine regimens have been approved for use in outbreak scenarios, including the Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA‐BN‐Filo (Zabdeno/Mvabea) two-dose vaccine, where the MVA-BN-Filo booster dose contains EBOV, MARV, and Sudan (SUDV) virus glycoproteins (GPs) and the nucleoprotein from Tai Forest virus. While long-term immunogenicity of up to two years has been found in clinical trial settings, limited real-world data exists. Methods: Using a multiplexed immunoassay, samples (n=698 at baseline) collected in Mbandaka, Equateur province, DRC, between September 2023 and October 2024 were assessed for seroreactivity to six filovirus antigens (1 BDBV, 2 EBOV, 2 MARV, and 1 SUDV) at three distinct periods: baseline/pre-vaccination, 6-8 weeks post-first dose (Zabdeno), at booster administration (Mvabea), and one-year post-boost dose. Results: Substantial filovirus seroreactivity was found at baseline, with 48.7% (n=340/698) of individuals being seroreactive to at least one virus antigen. High baseline seroreactivity was found against BDBV GP (31.1%, n=217/698), with lower baseline seroreactivity to EBOV GP (15.5%, n=106/698), comparatively. Overall EBOV GP seroreactivity increased to 66.8% (n=376/563) at one year-post vaccine boost and 57.6% (n=250/434) of participants were seroreactive. Despite the booster dose inclusion of SUDV GP and MARV GP, there were no substantial increases in reactivity against either antigen at subsequent timepoints. Overall filovirus seroreactivity increased at all timepoints for the entire cohort, although filovirus reactivity decreased over the study period for those who were seroreactive at baseline. Findings: These data highlight detection of significantly elevated seoreactivity to EBOV GP following first-dose administration of Ad26.ZEBOV, which remained relatively stable one-year post-booster dose administration. Additionally, this study identifies high levels of baseline seroreactivity to BDBV GP despite no previous documented outbreaks in this region of DRC. These data suggest that vaccination with the Ad26.ZEBOV-MVA-BN-Filo vaccine induces stable seroreactivity against EBOV GP, but not to other filovirus antigens.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo 疫苗在刚果民主共和国(DRC)人群中长期的免疫原性,该地区丝状病毒血清反应性较为普遍。鉴于现有数据有限,本研究还针对疫苗的效力获取真实世界数据的需求进行了探讨。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于2023年9月至2024年10月在刚果民主共和国埃奎托尔省姆班达卡开展。研究共纳入698名参与者,评估了他们在基线、首次接种后6-8周以及加强接种后一年时对六种丝状病毒抗原的血清学反应性。
elements_zh.methods: 血清反应性通过多重免疫分析检测评估。样本来自接受过Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo 疫苗方案的个体,该方案包括含有埃博拉病毒(EBOV)、马尔堡病毒(MARV)和萨伊病毒(SUDV)GP蛋白以及来自泰森林病毒的核蛋白的MVA-BN-Filo加强剂。
elements_zh.main_results: 基线时,48.7%的参与者对至少一种丝状病毒抗原呈血清学反应。在加强剂量后一年,埃博拉病毒GP的血清学反应率增加至66.8%,而对SUDV GP和MARV GP的反应率没有显著增加。总体丝状病毒血清学反应率在所有时间点均有所上升,但对于基线时已呈血清学反应的个体,其反应率则下降。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究发现,Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo 疫苗能够诱导针对EBOV GP的稳定血清反应,但不会对其他丝状病毒抗原产生反应。同时观察到对BDBV GP有较高的基线血清反应性,尽管该地区此前未有记录的暴发病例。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,疫苗在诱导针对EBOV GP的长期血清反应性方面是有效的,这对于监测和早期检测EBOV 暴发至关重要。然而,缺乏对其他丝状病毒抗原的增强反应性表明需要额外的疫苗或加强策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的设计局限性包括缺乏对照组以及可能存在混杂因素。由于研究的观察性质和样本量有限,证据强度为中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo 疫苗在刚果民主共和国(DRC)人群中长期的免疫原性,该地区丝状病毒血清反应性较为普遍。鉴于现有数据有限,本研究还针对疫苗的效力获取真实世界数据的需求进行了探讨。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于2023年9月至2024年10月在刚果民主共和国埃奎托尔省姆班达卡开展。研究共纳入698名参与者,评估了他们在基线、首次接种后6-8周以及加强接种后一年时对六种丝状病毒抗原的血清学反应性。
analysis_zh.methods: 血清反应性通过多重免疫分析检测评估。样本来自接受过Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo 疫苗方案的个体,该方案包括含有埃博拉病毒(EBOV)、马尔堡病毒(MARV)和萨伊病毒(SUDV)GP蛋白以及来自泰森林病毒的核蛋白的MVA-BN-Filo加强剂。
analysis_zh.main_results: 基线时,48.7%的参与者对至少一种丝状病毒抗原呈血清学反应。在加强剂量后一年,埃博拉病毒GP的血清学反应率增加至66.8%,而对SUDV GP和MARV GP的反应率没有显著增加。总体丝状病毒血清学反应率在所有时间点均有所上升,但对于基线时已呈血清学反应的个体,其反应率则下降。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究发现,Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo 疫苗能够诱导针对EBOV GP的稳定血清反应,但不会对其他丝状病毒抗原产生反应。同时观察到对BDBV GP有较高的基线血清反应性,尽管该地区此前未有记录的暴发病例。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,疫苗在诱导针对EBOV GP的长期血清反应性方面是有效的,这对于监测和早期检测EBOV 暴发至关重要。然而,缺乏对其他丝状病毒抗原的增强反应性表明需要额外的疫苗或加强策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的设计局限性包括缺乏对照组以及可能存在混杂因素。由于研究的观察性质和样本量有限,证据强度为中等。

title: Ebola Virus Disease in Pregnancy: Maternal–Fetal Outcomes, Vertical Transmission, and Implications for Vaccination—A Narrative Review
abstract: Background/Objectives: Ebola virus disease (EVD) during pregnancy is associated with severe maternal illness and exceptionally poor fetal and neonatal outcomes. However, pregnancy-specific evidence remains limited by small cohorts, heterogeneous outbreak settings, and the historical exclusion of pregnant women from clinical research. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes, placental involvement and vertical transmission, clinical management, and vaccination during pregnancy. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through May 2026 using predefined terms related to EVD, pregnancy, maternal and neonatal outcomes, placental infection, vertical transmission, and vaccination. WHO and CDC guidance documents and reference lists of relevant publications were also reviewed. Two reviewers independently screened records and assessed full texts. Data was extracted using a standardized template and independently verified by a second reviewer. A total of 55 publications met the inclusion criteria and were narratively synthesized. Results: Historical reports documented very high maternal mortality and pregnancy loss; however, more recent studies do not indicate that pregnancy independently increases maternal mortality among patients with EVD. A systematic review and meta-analysis estimated maternal mortality at 67.8% (95% CI 49.8–83.7), fetal loss at 76.9% (95% CI 45.0–98.3), and neonatal mortality at 98.5% (95% CI 84.9–100). Contemporary data from the 2018–2020 Democratic Republic of the Congo outbreak similarly found no increased maternal mortality associated with pregnancy, although fetal and perinatal outcomes remained poor. Evidence supports placental involvement in EVD, but placental viral RNA detection should be distinguished from confirmed fetal or neonatal infection. Pregnancy-specific vaccine evidence now includes a Phase 3 trial of Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo in 2013 pregnant women, demonstrating favorable safety and immunogenicity profiles. Conclusions: EVD in pregnancy remains associated with substantial pregnancy loss and neonatal mortality despite improvements in maternal care. Important gaps persist regarding maternal–fetal transmission, long-term infant outcomes, and optimal management strategies, highlighting the need for further research.

title: Identification of Host Gene Transcripts by Machine Learning and Their Application to Predict Outcome in Ebola Virus Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In humans, Ebola virus disease (EVD) has a high mortality rate. While viral load is a known prognostic factor, it is not effective in predicting outcomes across all patients. Exploring host transcriptomic signatures may provide additional predictive value. METHODS: Here, the transcript abundance of 4 candidate host genes (VCAM1, TUBG1, MS4A4A, ISG15) was quantified by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) in blood samples from hospitalized patients with Ebola virus (EBOV) collected during the 2013-2016 West African outbreak. Samples were taken for diagnostic purposes during the acute phase of infection. Associations between target gene expression, viral load, and outcome (survival/death) were assessed, and machine learning models were trained and tested to predict patient outcome. RESULTS: EBOV cycle threshold (Ct) values were significantly higher in hospitalized survivors compared to fatalities. During the acute phase, the transcript abundance of VCAM1 and MS4A4A was higher in fatal cases, while TUBG1 expression was elevated in survivors; ISG15 expression did not differ by outcome. In support vector machine models, EBOV Ct alone classified patient outcomes with 86.9% accuracy, while MS4A4A alone reached 82.6%. Combining EBOV Ct with MS4A4A improved prediction to 91.3%. The best-performing model, integrating EBOV Ct, ISG15, and MS4A4A, achieved 100% accuracy in the test set. DISCUSSION: Host gene expression markers, particularly MS4A4A, in combination with viral load, improved outcome prediction in EVD beyond viral load alone in ambiguous cases with mid-range Ct values. These findings highlight the utility of host transcript-based assays to inform clinical management and for benchmarking the effectiveness of medical countermeasures during outbreaks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 埃博拉病毒病 (埃博拉病毒病) 具有较高的 死亡率 率,尽管病毒载量是已知的预后因素,但它在所有患者中并不有效预测结果。探索 宿主 转录组特征可能提供额外的预测价值。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在2013-2016年西非埃博拉病毒暴发期间收集的住院患者急性感染期样本,用于诊断目的。
elements_zh.methods: 通过对血液样本进行逆转录定量聚合酶链反应(RT-qPCR),量化了4个候选宿主基因(VCAM1、TUBG1、MS4A4A、ISG15)的转录丰度。评估了目标基因表达、病毒载量与结果(生存/死亡)之间的关联,并训练和测试了机器学习模型以预测患者结果。
elements_zh.main_results: 埃博拉病毒(EBOV)的循环阈值(Ct)值在住院幸存者中显著高于死亡病例。在急性期,致命病例中VCAM1和MS4A4A的转录丰度较高,而TUBG1的表达在幸存者中升高;ISG15的表达在不同结果之间没有差异。支持媒介机器模型,单独使用EBOV Ct可对患者结果进行86.9%准确率的分类,而单独使用MS4A4A则达到82.6%。将EBOV Ct与MS4A4A结合后,预测准确率提高至91.3%。表现最好的模型,整合了EBOV Ct、ISG15和MS4A4A,其在测试集中的准确率为100%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 宿主基因表达标志物,特别是MS4A4A,在结合病毒载量的情况下,相较于单独使用病毒载量,在Ct值处于中等范围的埃博拉病毒病(EVD)模糊病例中提高了预后预测效果。这些发现凸显了基于暴发转录物的检测方法在指导临床管理以及评估医疗应对措施有效性中的价值。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,基于宿主转录本的检测方法可以改善临床管理,并有助于在埃博拉病毒病 暴发期间评估医疗应对措施的有效性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于特定暴发时期住院患者,因此结果可能无法推广至所有埃博拉病毒病病例。由于特定背景和有限的人群,证据强度为中等。

abstract_zh: 背景:在人类中,埃博拉病毒病(埃博拉病毒病,EVD)具有高死亡率率。尽管病毒载量是已知的预后因素,但它在预测所有患者预后方面并不有效。探索宿主转录组特征可能提供额外的预测价值。方法:在此研究中,通过逆转录定量聚合酶链反应(RT-qPCR)在2013-2016年西非暴发期间收集的住院埃博拉病毒(埃博拉病毒,EBOV)患者血液样本中,量化了4个候选宿主基因(VCAM1、TUBG1、MS4A4A、ISG15)的转录丰度。在感染急性期采集样本用于诊断。评估了目标基因表达、病毒载量与预后(存活/死亡)之间的关联,并训练和测试机器学习模型以预测患者预后。结果:住院存活者的埃博拉病毒(EBOV)循环阈值(Ct)值显著高于死亡者。在急性期,VCAM1和MS4A4A的转录丰度在死亡病例中更高,而TUBG1表达在存活者中升高;ISG15表达在预后上无差异。支持媒介机器模型的数据显示,单独使用EBOV Ct值可对患者预后进行86.9%的准确分类,而单独使用MS4A4A则达到82.6%。将EBOV Ct与MS4A4A结合后,预测准确率提高至91.3%。表现最佳的模型,整合了EBOV Ct、ISG15和MS4A4A,其测试集准确率达到100%。讨论:在Ct值处于中等范围的不确定病例中,结合宿主基因表达标志物(特别是MS4A4A)与病毒载量,可提高埃博拉病毒病(EVD)预后预测的准确性,超越仅依赖病毒载量的预测效果。这些发现凸显了基于宿主转录本的检测方法在临床管理以及在暴发期间评估医疗干预措施有效性方面的实用性。科学与公共卫生意义:这些发现表明,基于宿主转录本的检测方法可能有助于改善临床管理,并在埃博拉病毒病 暴发期间评估医疗干预措施的有效性。局限性与证据强度:本研究仅限于特定暴发期间住院患者,因此结果可能无法推广到所有埃博拉病毒病(EVD)病例。由于特定背景和有限人群,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 埃博拉病毒病 (埃博拉病毒病) 具有较高的 死亡率 率,尽管病毒载量是已知的预后因素,但它在所有患者中并不有效预测结果。探索 宿主 转录组特征可能提供额外的预测价值。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在2013-2016年西非埃博拉病毒暴发期间收集的住院患者急性感染期样本,用于诊断目的。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过对血液样本进行逆转录定量聚合酶链反应(RT-qPCR),量化了4个候选宿主基因(VCAM1、TUBG1、MS4A4A、ISG15)的转录丰度。评估了目标基因表达、病毒载量与结果(生存/死亡)之间的关联,并训练和测试了机器学习模型以预测患者结果。
analysis_zh.main_results: 埃博拉病毒(EBOV)的循环阈值(Ct)值在住院幸存者中显著高于死亡病例。在急性期,致命病例中VCAM1和MS4A4A的转录丰度较高,而TUBG1的表达在幸存者中升高;ISG15的表达在不同结果之间没有差异。支持媒介机器模型,单独使用EBOV Ct可对患者结果进行86.9%准确率的分类,而单独使用MS4A4A则达到82.6%。将EBOV Ct与MS4A4A结合后,预测准确率提高至91.3%。表现最好的模型,整合了EBOV Ct、ISG15和MS4A4A,其在测试集中的准确率为100%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 宿主基因表达标志物,特别是MS4A4A,在结合病毒载量的情况下,相较于单独使用病毒载量,在Ct值处于中等范围的埃博拉病毒病(EVD)模糊病例中提高了预后预测效果。这些发现凸显了基于暴发转录物的检测方法在指导临床管理以及评估医疗应对措施有效性中的价值。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,基于宿主转录本的检测方法可以改善临床管理,并有助于在埃博拉病毒病 暴发期间评估医疗应对措施的有效性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于特定暴发时期住院患者,因此结果可能无法推广至所有埃博拉病毒病病例。由于特定背景和有限的人群,证据强度为中等。

title: Molecular Phenotypes of Sex- and Age-Specific Differences Relating to Outcome in Patients With Ebola Virus Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ebola virus causes a severe, potentially fatal disease with the outcome likely related to viral and host factors. There is a clear correlation between viral load and outcome (survival/death), and inflammatory and other cellular pathways are differentially activated in the acute stage between patients who survive and those who die. Age and sex may influence the course of Ebola virus disease with potential differences at the molecular level. METHODS: To investigate whether there were age- and/or sex-specific differences in patients with Ebola virus disease, previously published data from an RNA sequencing analysis of the blood transcriptome in patients from the 2013-2016 West African outbreak were stratified according to age and sex. This was correlated with the outcome of infection. RESULTS: Similar to the previously published data, immune responses were downregulated during the acute phase in hospitalized survivors as compared with hospitalized fatal cases, regardless of the sex of the patient. However, aspects of the blood transcriptome/host response differed between females and males and certain age groups at the transcriptomic level. Genes associated with the lymphocyte differentiation pathway decreased in expression level with age in hospitalized fatal cases. However, this was the opposite in hospitalized survivors. CONCLUSIONS: From a medical countermeasure perspective, the work indicated that selection of animal models should consider age and sex, depending on the research question, and cellular pathways were identified that could be chemotherapeutically enhanced to promote survival.

abstract_zh: 背景:埃博拉病毒会导致一种严重的、可能致命的疾病,其预后可能与病毒和宿主因素相关。病毒载量与预后(存活/死亡)之间存在明显的相关性,并且在急性期,存活患者与死亡患者的炎症和其他细胞通路的激活情况存在差异。年龄和性别可能影响埃博拉病毒病的病程,并可能在分子层面上存在差异。方法:为了研究埃博拉病毒病患者是否存在年龄和/或性别特异性差异,对2013-2016年西非暴发患者的血液转录组进行的RNA测序分析数据,按照年龄和性别进行分层。这些数据与感染的预后相关联。结果:与之前发表的数据相似,在住院存活患者中,免疫应答在急性期的表达水平低于住院死亡患者,无论患者的性别如何。然而,在血液转录组/宿主反应方面,女性和男性以及某些年龄组之间存在差异。与淋巴细胞分化通路相关的基因在住院死亡患者中随年龄增长而表达水平下降,但在住院存活患者中则相反。结论:从医疗对策的角度来看,这项研究表明,根据研究问题选择动物模型时应考虑年龄和性别。同时,识别出了一些可以用于化疗增强以促进存活的细胞通路。

title: Barriers and Facilitators to Adopting Safe Burial Practices During the 2014–2016 Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak in Liberia: A 2024 Retrospective Mixed-Methods Study
abstract: Traditional funeral practices were a significant factor in the transmission of Ebola virus disease (EVD) during the West African outbreak of 2014–2016. In Liberia, these practices often conflict with public health directives, resulting in noncompliance and secret burials. Understanding the barriers to and facilitators of adopting safe burial practices is critical for informing future epidemic responses. This mixed-methods study was conducted in Vai and Clara Towns, Monrovia, Liberia. Data collection included surveys (n = 200), in-depth interviews (n = 40), and four focus groups (n = 40) with family members and community leaders. The quantitative data was analyzed via descriptive statistics. Thematic analysis was applied to the qualitative data to identify major themes. The survey demonstrated high levels of EVD-related knowledge and perceived risk in 2024; however, these descriptive findings do not establish an association between knowledge and burial behavior. Qualitative findings identified cultural, emotional, social, informational, and logistical factors that influenced the adoption of safe burial practices during the outbreak. Qualitative analysis revealed seven major themes: cultural and traditional resistance, mistrust and stigma, misinformation, emotional and psychological distress, communication and logistical challenges, socioeconomic constraints, and facilitators of safe practices. Knowledge measured in 2024 cannot establish outbreak-era knowledge. Retrospective accounts identified cultural norms, mistrust, and systemic barriers to safe burials. Future responses should prioritize early community engagement, the involvement of traditional and religious leaders, culturally sensitive adaptations of protocols, and adequate psychosocial and logistical support.
journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health

analysis.summary_en: This 2024 retrospective mixed-methods study in Liberia aimed to understand the barriers and facilitators to adopting safe burial practices during the 2014–2016 Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 传统的葬礼习俗是2014–2016年西非暴发期间埃博拉病毒病(埃博拉病毒病)传播的重要因素。了解采用安全葬礼实践的障碍与促进因素对于制定未来的疫情应对措施至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本混合方法研究在利比里亚蒙罗维亚的Vai和Clara镇进行。数据收集包括200份调查问卷、40次深入访谈以及与家庭成员和社区领袖进行的4次焦点小组讨论。
elements_zh.methods: 定量数据通过描述性统计进行分析,定性数据则通过主题分析来识别主要主题。
elements_zh.main_results: 调查显示,2024年人们对埃博拉病毒相关知识和感知风险较高;然而,这些描述性发现并不能证明知识与葬礼行为之间的关联。定性分析揭示了七个主要主题:文化与传统阻力、不信任与污名、错误信息、情绪与心理压力、沟通与物流挑战、社会经济限制以及安全实践的促进因素。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 定性分析指出了影响疫情期间采用安全葬礼实践的文化、情感、社会、信息和物流因素。本研究强调了在未来疫情应对中解决这些因素的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 未来的应对措施应优先考虑早期社区参与、传统和宗教领袖的参与、对协议的文化敏感性调整以及充分的心理社会和物流支持。这些发现可以为制定更有效的公共卫生策略以管理暴发提供依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 2024年测量的知识无法代表暴发时期的知识。本研究依赖于回顾性叙述,这可能会引入偏倚并限制研究结果的准确性。

analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Future responses should prioritize early community engagement, the involvement of traditional and religious leaders, culturally sensitive adaptations of protocols, and adequate psychosocial and logistical support. These findings can inform the development of more effective public health strategies for managing outbreaks.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Knowledge measured in 2024 cannot establish outbreak-era knowledge. The study relies on retrospective accounts, which may introduce bias and limit the accuracy of the findings.

title_zh: 2014–2016年利比里亚埃博拉病毒病(埃博拉病毒病)疫情期间采用安全葬礼实践的障碍与促进因素:2024年回顾性混合方法研究
source_body_en: Traditional funeral practices were a significant factor in the transmission of Ebola virus disease (EVD) during the West African outbreak of 2014–2016. In Liberia, these practices often conflict with public health directives, resulting in noncompliance and secret burials. Understanding the barriers to and facilitators of adopting safe burial practices is critical for informing future epidemic responses. This mixed-methods study was conducted in Vai and Clara Towns, Monrovia, Liberia. Data collection included surveys (n = 200), in-depth interviews (n = 40), and four focus groups (n = 40) with family members and community leaders. The quantitative data was analyzed via descriptive statistics. Thematic analysis was applied to the qualitative data to identify major themes. The survey demonstrated high levels of EVD-related knowledge and perceived risk in 2024; however, these descriptive findings do not establish an association between knowledge and burial behavior. Qualitative findings identified cultural, emotional, social, informational, and logistical factors that influenced the adoption of safe burial practices during the outbreak. Qualitative analysis revealed seven major themes: cultural and traditional resistance, mistrust and stigma, misinformation, emotional and psychological distress, communication and logistical challenges, socioeconomic constraints, and facilitators of safe practices. Knowledge measured in 2024 cannot establish outbreak-era knowledge. Retrospective accounts identified cultural norms, mistrust, and systemic barriers to safe burials. Future responses should prioritize early community engagement, the involvement of traditional and religious leaders, culturally sensitive adaptations of protocols, and adequate psychosocial and logistical support.
abstract_zh: 传统的葬礼习俗是2014–2016年西非暴发期间埃博拉病毒病(埃博拉病毒病)传播的重要因素。在利比里亚,这些习俗常常与公共卫生指导相冲突,导致不遵守规定和秘密葬礼。了解采用安全葬礼实践的障碍与促进因素对于制定未来的疫情应对措施至关重要。本混合方法研究在利比里亚蒙罗维亚的Vai和Clara镇进行。数据收集包括200份调查问卷、40次深入访谈以及与家庭成员和社区领袖进行的4次焦点小组讨论。定量数据通过描述性统计进行分析,定性数据则通过主题分析来识别主要主题。调查显示,2024年人们对埃博拉病毒相关知识和感知风险较高;然而,这些描述性发现并不能证明知识与葬礼行为之间的关联。定性分析揭示了七个主要主题:文化与传统阻力、不信任与污名、错误信息、情绪与心理压力、沟通与物流挑战、社会经济限制以及安全实践的促进因素。2024年测量的知识无法代表暴发时期的知识。回顾性叙述指出了文化规范、不信任和安全葬礼的系统性障碍。未来的应对措施应优先考虑早期社区参与、传统和宗教领袖的参与、对协议的文化敏感性调整以及充分的心理社会和物流支持。

title: Whole-genome phylogenetic and population genetic analysis of Orthoebolavirus restonense
abstract: Introduction Orthoebolavirus restonense (Reston virus; RESTV) is a zoonotic virus that has been detected primarily in non-human primates and swine. Despite its recognized public health importance, the evolutionary dynamics and population structure of RESTV remain poorly understood. Methods In this study, we conducted an in silico analysis of 20 publicly available RESTV whole-genome sequences to build upon previous analyses by updating phylogenetic relationships, evolutionary timescales, and incorporating additional analyses of genetic diversity and population subdivision across host groups and outbreak periods. Results Maximum-likelihood and Bayesian analyses support 5 multi-sequence clusters and 2 phylogenetically distinct singleton lineages. The common ancestor of the sampled genomes was estimated around 1967, with a broad 95% highest posterior density interval of 1930–1988, indicating that the sampled evolutionary history likely predates the first recognized outbreak in 1989. The pooled dataset showed high haplotype diversity, while swine-derived genomes exhibited greater nucleotide diversity than primate-derived genomes. Furthermore, neutrality tests based on the limited number of genomes (n=20) did not detect evidence of recent rapid population expansion. Discussion Population structure analyses suggest structured, highly divergent viral sequences, with temporal segregation exerting a greater influence than host-associated factors, although the relative contributions of outbreak period and host are difficult to disentangle due to the uneven distribution of hosts across sampling periods. The estimated ancestry of sampled genomes predating the first recognized outbreak, together with the evidence of population structure, raises the possibility of earlier undetected, potentially cryptic circulation; however, responsible host(s), and continuity of transmission remain unresolved. Nevertheless, the limited number of available genome sequences constrains a comprehensive understanding of RESTV evolutionary history and transmission dynamics. Expanded genomic surveillance and One Health integration are therefore essential to better elucidate the virus’ evolution, epidemiology, and zoonotic potential.

abstract_zh: 引言 Orthoebolavirus restonense(Reston病毒;RESTV)是一种人兽共患病病毒,主要在非人类灵长类动物和猪中被检测到。尽管其被广泛认为具有重要的公共卫生意义,但RESTV的进化动态和群体结构仍知之甚少。方法 本研究对20个公开可用的RESTV全基因组序列进行了计算机模拟分析,以更新系统发育关系、进化时间尺度,并进一步分析基因组群体在宿主群体和暴发时期内的遗传多样性及群体分化。结果 最大似然法和贝叶斯分析支持5个多序列簇和2个系统发育上不同的单序列谱系。所采样基因组的共同祖先估计约为1967年,其95%最高后验密度区间为1930–1988年,表明所采样的进化历史可能早于1989年首次被记录的暴发。合并数据集显示高单倍型多样性,而来源于猪的基因组表现出比来源于灵长类动物的基因组更高的核苷酸多样性。此外,基于有限数量的基因组(n=20)进行的中性检验未发现近期快速群体扩张的证据。讨论 群体结构分析表明,病毒序列具有结构化且高度分歧的特征,时间隔离的影响大于与宿主相关的因素,但由于宿主在采样时期分布不均,暴发时期和宿主的相对贡献难以区分。所采样基因组的祖先估计早于首次记录的暴发,结合群体结构的证据,提出了RESTV可能更早存在未被检测到的潜在隐匿传播的可能性;然而,具体负责的宿主(s)以及传播的连续性仍不清楚。尽管如此,可用的基因组序列数量有限,限制了对RESTV进化历史和传播动态的全面理解。因此,扩大基因组监测和One Health整合对于更好地阐明该病毒的进化、流行病学和人兽共患病潜力至关重要。

title: Assessing the Risk for Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak and Health System Response Capacity in Conflict-Affected Sudan
abstract: Background: Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) is a severe viral hemorrhagic fever with high case fatality rates. Ongoing regional outbreaks in Uganda and the DRC, combined with protracted armed conflict in Sudan since April 2023, increase vulnerability to importation and spread, putting Sudan at risk. Conflict has caused widespread health infrastructure destruction, healthcare worker displacement, and disruption of surveillance and laboratory systems. This study assesses Sudan’s risk of an EVD outbreak and national response capacity in the context of conflict. Methods: We reviewed peer-reviewed and grey literature using PubMed, Medline, Google Scholar, WHO, CDC, UNICEF, and UN OCHA reports. No time restrictions were applied. We applied a SWOT analysis framework to classify factors influencing EVD prevention, detection, preparedness, and response in conflict-affected Sudan. The analysis focused on health system functionality, surveillance, laboratory capacity, workforce, and population vulnerabilities. Results: Our study found existing strengths, including availability of national EVD preparedness plans, prior experience responding to cholera, dengue, measles, and COVID-19, functional coordination through the Health Cluster, and ongoing disease surveillance systems including EWARS and Event-Based Surveillance. Weaknesses identified include severe disruption of health services (48% of facilities fully functional), health workforce shortages and burnout, disruption of laboratory capacity, and surveillance and access constraints in conflict-affected areas of Darfur and Kordofan. The ongoing health security frameworks, including the National Health Policy, National Health Sector Recovery Plan, and regional cross-border initiatives, expansion of digital surveillance, laboratory decentralization efforts, and recent international investments in health system recovery, provide significant opportunities for optimal preparedness and response. Threats identified include continued armed conflict and insecurity, large-scale internal displacement and cross-border mobility, humanitarian access constraints, and funding instability. Geographic risk synthesis indicates Darfur is at the highest risk for delayed detection and silent transmission, Kordofan serves as a transmission corridor, and Khartoum faces the highest risk of urban amplification. Conclusion: Sudan faces a moderate to high EVD outbreak risk due to potential virus importation, a conflict-weakened health system, and mass displacement. Key priorities: strengthen EWARS in conflict zones, decentralize laboratory capacity, restore health facilities with strong IPC, build workforce capacity, and adopt mobility-informed preparedness. Peace and international support remain essential for effective EVD response.

title_zh: 评估埃博拉病毒病 暴发对苏丹健康系统响应能力的风险
source_body_en: Background: Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) is a severe viral hemorrhagic fever with high case fatality rates. Ongoing regional outbreaks in Uganda and the DRC, combined with protracted armed conflict in Sudan since April 2023, increase vulnerability to importation and spread, putting Sudan at risk. Conflict has caused widespread health infrastructure destruction, healthcare worker displacement, and disruption of surveillance and laboratory systems. This study assesses Sudan’s risk of an EVD outbreak and national response capacity in the context of conflict. Methods: We reviewed peer-reviewed and grey literature using PubMed, Medline, Google Scholar, WHO, CDC, UNICEF, and UN OCHA reports. No time restrictions were applied. We applied a SWOT analysis framework to classify factors influencing EVD prevention, detection, preparedness, and response in conflict-affected Sudan. The analysis focused on health system functionality, surveillance, laboratory capacity, workforce, and population vulnerabilities. Results: Our study found existing strengths, including availability of national EVD preparedness plans, prior experience responding to cholera, dengue, measles, and COVID-19, functional coordination through the Health Cluster, and ongoing disease surveillance systems including EWARS and Event-Based Surveillance. Weaknesses identified include severe disruption of health services (48% of facilities fully functional), health workforce shortages and burnout, disruption of laboratory capacity, and surveillance and access constraints in conflict-affected areas of Darfur and Kordofan. The ongoing health security frameworks, including the National Health Policy, National Health Sector Recovery Plan, and regional cross-border initiatives, expansion of digital surveillance, laboratory decentralization efforts, and recent international investments in health system recovery, provide significant opportunities for optimal preparedness and response. Threats identified include continued armed conflict and insecurity, large-scale internal displacement and cross-border mobility, humanitarian access constraints, and funding instability. Geographic risk synthesis indicates Darfur is at the highest risk for delayed detection and silent transmission, Kordofan serves as a transmission corridor, and Khartoum faces the highest risk of urban amplification. Conclusion: Sudan faces a moderate to high EVD outbreak risk due to potential virus importation, a conflict-weakened health system, and mass displacement. Key priorities: strengthen EWARS in conflict zones, decentralize laboratory capacity, restore health facilities with strong IPC, build workforce capacity, and adopt mobility-informed preparedness. Peace and international support remain essential for effective EVD response.
abstract_zh: 背景:埃博拉病毒病(埃博拉病毒病EVD)是一种严重的病毒性出血热,病死率高。乌干达和刚果民主共和国持续的暴发,以及苏丹自2023年4月以来的长期武装冲突,增加了病毒引入和传播的风险,使苏丹面临风险。冲突导致广泛的卫生基础设施破坏、医护人员流失以及监测和实验室系统的中断。本研究评估了冲突背景下苏丹的EVD 暴发风险及其国家应对能力。方法:我们查阅了PubMed、Medline、Google Scholar、WHO、CDC、UNICEF和UN OCHA的同行评审和灰色文献。未施加时间限制。我们应用SWOT分析框架来分类影响冲突地区EVD预防、检测、准备和应对的因素。分析重点包括卫生系统功能、监测、实验室能力、劳动力和人群脆弱性。结果:我们的研究发现了一些优势,包括国家EVD准备计划的可用性、对霍乱、登革热、麻疹和COVID-19的应对经验、通过卫生集群的功能性协调、以及包括EWARS和事件驱动监测在内的持续疾病监测系统。识别出的弱点包括卫生服务严重中断(48%的设施完全功能)、卫生人员短缺和倦怠、实验室能力中断、以及在达尔富尔和科尔多凡受冲突影响地区的监测和访问限制。包括国家卫生政策、国家卫生部门恢复计划和区域跨境倡议在内的持续卫生安全框架,以及数字监测的扩展、实验室去中心化努力和最近的国际卫生系统恢复投资,提供了显著的机会,以实现最佳准备和应对。识别出的威胁包括持续的武装冲突和不安全、大规模内部流离失所和跨境流动性、人道主义准入限制和资金不稳定。地理风险综合分析表明,达尔富尔面临延迟检测和无声传播的风险最高,科尔多凡作为传播走廊,喀土穆面临城市放大风险最高。结论:苏丹面临中等到高风险的EVD 暴发,由于潜在的病毒引入、冲突削弱的卫生系统和大规模流离失所。关键优先事项:在冲突地区加强EWARS,去中心化实验室能力,恢复卫生设施并强化感染预防与控制,建立劳动力能力,采用基于移动性的准备措施。和平与国际支持对于有效的EVD应对至关重要。

title: Ebola Disease Knowledge and Vaccine Acceptance in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
abstract: We report general acceptance (79.0%) of Ebola vaccination in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) between 2023-2024 (n=5,062). Acceptance varied significantly by province with acceptance ranging from 47.6% in Kongo Central to 92.1% in Tshuapa province and was highest among healthcare workers. While Ebola vaccine acceptance and disease knowledge are relatively strong nationally in the DRC, regional differences do exist and may impact future vaccine rollout.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focuses on Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, examining its epidemiological and clinical characteristics in these regions.
analysis.methods: The methods involve reviewing existing literature and data on Bundibugyo virus disease, with an emphasis on its occurrence and impact in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.
analysis.main_results: The study reports that Bundibugyo virus disease is a significant and under-recognized public health issue in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, with cases of viral hemorrhagic fever documented.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence of the ongoing threat posed by Bundibugyo virus disease, emphasizing its role as an emerging infectious disease and the need for increased attention.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of improving surveillance and response strategies for Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda to mitigate its public health impact.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on existing literature and does not include new data, which limits the strength of the evidence. However, it provides a comprehensive overview of the current understanding of Bundibugyo virus disease.

analysis.summary_en: This study highlights the significance of Bundibugyo virus disease as a neglected public health threat in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. It emphasizes the virus's classification as an emerging infectious disease and viral hemorrhagic fever, underscoring the need for improved surveillance and response strategies. The research is based on existing literature, which provides a broad understanding of the disease's epidemiological and clinical characteristics. While the study does not include new data, it contributes to the awareness of the ongoing public health challenges posed by this virus. The findings suggest that further targeted research and intervention are necessary to address the gaps in knowledge and enhance preparedness for future outbreaks.

title: Exploratory network-based modelling of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease importation and spread in Uganda using Displacement Tracking Matrix flow data
abstract: Background: The 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in Uganda, linked to the ongoing epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), spread through human mobility across borders and within the country. Existing modelling has provided regional level importation estimates but not district level operational guidance. We developed an exploratory, scenario based decision support model to characterise subnational importation and spread patterns. Methods: We constructed a directed, weighted mobility network using International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) flows collected from 15 to 24 May 2026 (11,245 observed movements) and the 2024 Uganda census. A stochastic metapopulation SEIR model was simulated over 90 days across 135 Ugandan districts and two DRC provinces. We evaluated three scenario assumptions: containment (R0 = 0.80), moderate (R0 = 1.35), and weak (R0 = 2.76); plus a one-factor-at-a-time analysis of nonpharmaceutical intervention (NPI) compliance. Global sensitivity analysis was performed using Morris elementary-effects screening and total order Sobol indices. Results: The mobility network was sparse (density 0.11), highly unequal (Gini 0.67), and modular (0.50). Kisoro had the highest import risk (in-strength 3,823) and export risk (out-strength 1,350). Under all three scenarios, the model projected similar cumulative case counts (median 20 to 21; pairwise Mann Whitney p < 0.05). Under containment, Kampala was the only district with a non-zero median (20 cases, 95% simulation interval 20 to 22); all other districts had a median of 0. Prediction-interval coverage against the early observed curve was 0.80. Conclusions: Under the containment assumptions of the model, rapid 7 1 7 implementation was associated with substantial containment, but this is scenario-specific and does not imply that NPIs are unnecessary. Border surveillance, nationwide preparedness, and community engagement remain essential. These projections should be treated as exploratory and require prospective field-based validation.

abstract_zh: 背景:2026年乌干达爆发的邦迪布古埃博拉暴发,与刚果民主共和国(DRC)持续的疫情通过跨境和国内的人类流动性传播。现有的模型提供了区域层面的输入估计,但没有提供区级的操作指导。我们开发了一个探索性的、基于情景的决策支持模型,以描述次国家层面的输入和传播模式。方法:我们利用国际移民组织(IOM)5月15日至24日收集的位移追踪矩阵(DTM)流动数据(共11,245次观察到的流动)和2024年乌干达人口普查数据,构建了一个有向、加权的流动性网络。一个随机的元种群SEIR模型在90天内模拟了乌干达135个区和刚果民主共和国两个省的疫情传播。我们评估了三种情景假设:控制(R0 = 0.80)、中等(R0 = 1.35)和较弱(R0 = 2.76);以及非药物干预(NPI)依从性的单因素分析。使用莫里斯基本效应筛选和总阶索伯尔指数进行了全局敏感性分析。结果:流动性网络稀疏(密度0.11),高度不平等(基尼系数0.67),并具有模块性(0.50)。基索罗区的输入风险最高(入度3,823),输出风险最高(出度1,350)。在所有三种情景下,模型预测的累计病例数相似(中位数20至21;成对曼-惠特尼p < 0.05)。在控制情景下,只有坎帕拉区的中位数非零(20例,95%模拟区间20至22);其他所有区的中位数均为0。预测区间与早期观察曲线的覆盖率为0.80。结论:在模型的控制假设下,快速7 1 7实施与显著的控制效果相关,但这只是情景特定的,并不意味着非药物干预措施是不必要的。边境监测、全国范围内的准备和社区参与仍然是关键。这些预测应被视为探索性的,并需要前瞻性实地验证。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 2026年乌干达布干迪古约埃博拉暴发与刚果民主共和国(DRC)的持续疫情有关,通过国界和国内的人口流动传播。现有模型提供了区域级别的进口估计,但没有提供区级的操作指导。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们开发了一个探索性、基于情景的决策支持模型,使用国际移民组织(IOM)的流离失所追踪矩阵(DTM)流动数据和2024年乌干达人口普查数据,以表征次国家级别的进口和传播模式。
analysis_zh.methods: 我们模拟了一个随机化元种群SEIR模型,跨越135个乌干达区和两个刚果民主共和国省份,进行了90天的模拟,并进行了全局敏感性分析,使用Morris基本效应筛选和总阶Sobol指数。
analysis_zh.main_results: 移动网络稀疏(密度0.11),高度不平等(基尼系数0.67),模块化(0.50)。基索罗区的进口风险最高(入强度3,823),出口风险最高(出强度1,350)。在所有三种情景下,模型预测相似的累计病例数(中位数20至21;两两曼惠特尼p<0.05)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在模型的控制假设下,快速实施与显著的控制相关,但这取决于情景,不意味着非药物干预措施是不必要的。这些预测应被视为探索性的,并需要前瞻性现场验证。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 边境监测、全国范围的准备和社区参与仍然是必不可少的。该模型为管理埃博拉病毒病的进口和传播提供了区级的见解,以供操作指导。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该模型是探索性的,需要前瞻性现场验证。设计限制包括使用稀疏和不平等的移动数据,这可能会影响预测的准确性。

title: Resurgence of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo: Lessons Learned and Future Directions.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains the global epicenter of Ebola virus disease (EVD), having experienced more than 15 outbreaks since the disease was first identified in 1976. The 2025 resurgence in Kasai Province, caused by Orthoebolavirus zairense, resulted in over 60 confirmed cases and a case fatality rate exceeding 65%, highlighting persistent vulnerabilities in outbreak preparedness and response despite previous control successes. This article examines the drivers, response strategies, and public health implications of the 2025 Ebola outbreak. METHODS: This perspective synthesizes evidence from publicly available reports, epidemiological updates, genomic surveillance findings, and guidance from national and international public health agencies to examine the epidemiological characteristics, health system challenges, response interventions, and lessons learned from the 2025 Ebola outbreak in the DRC. RESULTS: Genomic evidence suggested viral persistence in human reservoirs as a likely source of the outbreak. Delayed diagnosis due to limited laboratory capacity, reagent shortages, and slow sample transportation impeded timely case confirmation. Sociocultural factors, including unsafe burial practices, vaccine hesitancy, and community mistrust, further complicated containment efforts. The outbreak overwhelmed fragile health systems, with inadequate isolation facilities and personal protective equipment contributing to healthcare worker infections, which accounted for 10% of reported cases. Coordinated national and international interventions, including emergency response activation, ring vaccination with the rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP (Ervebo) vaccine, enhanced surveillance, contact tracing, infection prevention and control measures, and technical support from global partners, were instrumental in interrupting transmission. CONCLUSION: The 2025 Ebola outbreak demonstrates the continued threat of recurrent EVD in the DRC and underscores the need for resilient surveillance systems, decentralized laboratory capacity, sustained infection prevention and control measures, healthcare worker protection, meaningful community engagement, and strengthened regional collaboration. Integrating genomic surveillance and advancing vaccine research will be critical for improving epidemic preparedness and strengthening health security across Central Africa.

abstract_zh: 介绍: 刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 仍然是全球 埃博拉病毒病 (埃博拉病毒病) 的中心,自1976年该病首次被确认以来,出现了超过15个 暴发。2025年卡萨伊省的复发由赞比亚伊波拉病毒引起,导致超过60例确诊病例以及病死率超过65%,凸显了 暴发 的准备和应对的持续脆弱性,尽管之前的控制措施取得成功。本文考察2025年埃博拉 暴发 的驱动因素、应对策略及公共卫生意义。方法: 本视角综合了公开可得的报告、流行病学更新、基因组监测 发现、来自国家和国际公共卫生机构的指导,以考察流行病学特征、健康系统挑战、应对措施以及从2025年埃博拉 暴发 在刚果民主共和国中汲取的经验教训。结果: 基因组证据表明病毒在人类 储存宿主 中持续存在,可能是 暴发 的来源。延迟的 诊断 由于实验室容量有限、试剂短缺以及样本运输缓慢,阻碍了及时的病例确认。社会文化因素,包括不安全的埋葬方式、疫苗 的犹豫以及社区不信任,进一步复杂化了防控工作。暴发 淹没了脆弱的健康系统,且隔离设施不足且个人防护装备不足导致医护人员感染,这占报告病例的10%。国家和国际协同干预,包括紧急响应启动、环形疫苗接种 与 rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP (Ervebo) 疫苗 相结合、增强 监测、接触者追踪、感染防控措施以及全球合作伙伴的技术支持,对中断 传播 起到了关键作用。结论: 2025年埃博拉 暴发 表明 DRC 中持续存在的反复埃博拉病毒病威胁,并凸显了对强健 监测 系统的需求、分散的实验室容量、持续的感染防控措施、医护人员保护、有意义的社区参与以及加强区域合作。整合 基因组监测 并推进 疫苗 研究对于改善流行病准备和加强非洲中部的健康安全至关重要。

title: Targeting TMEM16F‐Driven Membrane Remodeling: A Promising Strategy for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Development
abstract: With the continuous rise of epidemics with potential for global threats, the need for antiviral drug development continues to be essential. Most drugs approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) are direct-acting agents (DAAs), targeting specific viral proteins, thus restricting the range of applications of the antiviral. Due to the constant evolution of viruses, DAAs regularly have to be optimized or modified to maintain their inhibitory effect against emerging resistant variants. An alternative therapeutic approach to DAAs are host-directed agents (HDAs) which instead target host processes to inhibit viral infection. They offer more potential for broad-spectrum use if the targeted host processes are conserved across viral families. They are also more resistant to viral mutations. However, research has to be done to identify such strategic host targets. Previous work done on TMEM16F, a cell membrane Ca2+-activated scramblase, has identified it as an interesting candidate for host-directed antiviral strategies. TMEM16F’s role in phosphatidylserine (PS) translocation from the inner leaflet of the cell membrane to the outer leaflet is essential for microvesicle secretion. However, research has shown TMEM16F can be hijacked by viruses, such as Ebola virus and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), for viral apoptotic mimicry and for cell fusion, respectively. By activating TMEM16F for PS translocation, membrane-derived viral envelopes may contain this phospholipid, enabling glycoprotein-independent viral entry and dissemination into a host. The extent to which different virus families utilize this scramblase for viral spread and immune evasion remains to be elucidated. Niclosamide, an FDA-approved anthelminthic drug, was found to inhibit TMEM16F scramblase activity. Drug screening also revealed antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2. While niclosamide has shown antiviral, antibacterial and anticancer potential, it has low bioavailability and can cause severe side effects at high dosage. Since TMEM16F’s 3D structure was resolved with cryo-electron microscopy along with niclosamide’s binding pocket, AI-driven drug analog design may be used to optimize the drug’s efficacy and minimize cytotoxicity. Thus, in this paper, we will consider whether targeting TMEM16F scramblase activity offers broad-spectrum antiviral potential and whether niclosamide can be repurposed and optimized as a pan-viral HDA.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The continuous rise of epidemics with potential for global threats necessitates the development of antiviral drugs. Most approved drugs are direct-acting agents (DAAs) targeting specific viral proteins, which restricts their applications. Research on host-directed agents (HDAs) targeting host processes for broad-spectrum antiviral strategies is needed, especially since HDAs are more resistant to viral mutations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study aims to explore the potential of targeting TMEM16F, a cell membrane Ca2+-activated scramblase, for broad-spectrum antiviral development. TMEM16F’s role in phosphatidylserine (PS) translocation is essential for microvesicle secretion and can be hijacked by viruses for viral spread and immune evasion.
analysis.methods: TMEM16F’s 3D structure was resolved with cryo-electron microscopy, and niclosamide, an FDA-approved anthelminthic drug, was found to inhibit TMEM16F scramblase activity. Drug screening revealed antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2, and AI-driven drug analog design may be used to optimize niclosamide’s efficacy and minimize cytotoxicity.
analysis.main_results: Niclosamide inhibits TMEM16F scramblase activity and shows antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2. However, niclosamide has low bioavailability and can cause severe side effects at high dosage.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: TMEM16F’s role in viral spread and immune evasion is crucial, and targeting its scramblase activity offers broad-spectrum antiviral potential. Niclosamide can be repurposed and optimized as a pan-viral HDA.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Targeting TMEM16F scramblase activity could provide a broad-spectrum antiviral strategy. Further research is needed to identify strategic host targets and optimize niclosamide for clinical use.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the low bioavailability and potential side effects of niclosamide. The extent to which different virus families utilize TMEM16F for viral spread and immune evasion remains to be elucidated.

analysis.summary_en: The study explores the potential of targeting TMEM16F, a cell membrane Ca2+-activated scramblase, for broad-spectrum antiviral development. TMEM16F’s role in viral spread and immune evasion is crucial, and targeting its scramblase activity offers broad-spectrum antiviral potential. Niclosamide, an FDA-approved anthelminthic drug, inhibits TMEM16F scramblase activity and shows antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2, but further research is needed to optimize its efficacy and minimize side effects.

title_zh: 靶向TMEM16F驱动的膜重塑:一种具有广泛抗病毒潜力的策略
source_body_en: With the continuous rise of epidemics with potential for global threats, the need for antiviral drug development continues to be essential. Most drugs approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) are direct-acting agents (DAAs), targeting specific viral proteins, thus restricting the range of applications of the antiviral. Due to the constant evolution of viruses, DAAs regularly have to be optimized or modified to maintain their inhibitory effect against emerging resistant variants. An alternative therapeutic approach to DAAs are host-directed agents (HDAs) which instead target host processes to inhibit viral infection. They offer more potential for broad-spectrum use if the targeted host processes are conserved across viral families. They are also more resistant to viral mutations. However, research has to be done to identify such strategic host targets. Previous work done on TMEM16F, a cell membrane Ca2+-activated scramblase, has identified it as an interesting candidate for host-directed antiviral strategies. TMEM16F’s role in phosphatidylserine (PS) translocation from the inner leaflet of the cell membrane to the outer leaflet is essential for microvesicle secretion. However, research has shown TMEM16F can be hijacked by viruses, such as Ebola virus and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), for viral apoptotic mimicry and for cell fusion, respectively. By activating TMEM16F for PS translocation, membrane-derived viral envelopes may contain this phospholipid, enabling glycoprotein-independent viral entry and dissemination into a host. The extent to which different virus families utilize this scramblase for viral spread and immune evasion remains to be elucidated. Niclosamide, an FDA-approved anthelminthic drug, was found to inhibit TMEM16F scramblase activity. Drug screening also revealed antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2. While niclosamide has shown antiviral, antibacterial and anticancer potential, it has low bioavailability and can cause severe side effects at high dosage. Since TMEM16F’s 3D structure was resolved with cryo-electron microscopy along with niclosamide’s binding pocket, AI-driven drug analog design may be used to optimize the drug’s efficacy and minimize cytotoxicity. Thus, in this paper, we will consider whether targeting TMEM16F scramblase activity offers broad-spectrum antiviral potential and whether niclosamide can be repurposed and optimized as a pan-viral HDA.
abstract_zh: 随着可能对全球构成威胁的传染病持续增加,抗病毒药物药物开发的需求仍然至关重要。大多数由美国食品药品监督管理局(FDA)批准的药物是直接作用剂(DAAs),专门针对特定病毒蛋白,从而限制了抗病毒药物的应用范围。由于病毒的不断进化,DAAs需要定期优化或修改以维持其对新兴耐药变异体的抑制效果。DAAs之外的另一种治疗策略是宿主导向剂(HDAs),它们通过靶向宿主过程来抑制病毒感染。如果靶向的宿主过程在不同病毒家族中保守,它们将具有更广泛的适用性。此外,它们对病毒的耐受性也更强。然而,仍需进行研究以确定这样的战略宿主靶点。先前对TMEM16F的研究已将其识别为宿主导向抗病毒药物策略的有趣候选物。TMEM16F在磷脂酰丝氨酸(PS)从细胞膜内层转移到外层的转运中起着至关重要的作用,这是微泡分泌的关键。然而,研究表明,TMEM16F可以被病毒劫持,例如埃博拉病毒和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2),用于病毒凋亡模拟和细胞融合。通过激活TMEM16F进行PS转运,膜衍生的病毒包膜可能包含这种磷脂,从而实现不依赖糖蛋白的病毒进入和在宿主中的传播。不同病毒家族利用这种转位酶进行病毒传播和免疫逃避的程度仍需阐明。FDA批准的抗寄生虫药物尼克洛米德被发现可以抑制TMEM16F转位酶活性。药物筛选还揭示了尼克洛米德对SARS-CoV-2的抗病毒药物活性。尽管尼克洛米德显示出抗病毒药物、抗菌和抗癌潜力,但它生物利用度低,在高剂量下会引起严重副作用。由于TMEM16F的3D结构通过冷冻电子显微镜解析,并且已确定了尼克洛米德的结合口袋,因此可以利用AI驱动的药物类似物设计来优化药物的疗效并减少细胞毒性。因此,在本文中,我们将考虑靶向TMEM16F转位酶活性是否具有广泛的抗病毒药物潜力,以及尼克洛米德是否可以重新利用并优化为广谱HDA。

title: Improving the resolution and informativity of the majority-rule consensus tree using fine-grained dissimilarity measures.
abstract: Abstract Phylogenetic analyses often require the summarization of multiple trees, e.g., in Bayesian analyses to obtain the centroid of the posterior distribution of trees, or to determine the consensus of a set of bootstrap trees. The majority-rule consensus tree is the most commonly used. It is easy to compute and minimizes the sum of Robinson-Foulds (RF) distances to the input trees. In mathematical terms, the majority-rule consensus tree is the median of the input trees with respect to the RF distance. However, due to the coarse nature of RF distance, which only considers whether two branches induce exactly the same bipartition of the taxa or not, highly unresolved trees can be produced when the phylogenetic signal is low. To overcome this limitation, we propose using median trees with respect to finer-grained dissimilarity measures between trees. These measures include a quartet distance between tree topologies, and transfer distances, which quantify the similarity between bipartitions, in contrast to the presence/absence view of RF. We describe fast heuristic consensus algorithms for transfer-based tree dissimilarities, capable of efficiently processing trees with thousands of taxa. Through evaluations on simulated datasets in both Bayesian and bootstrapping maximum-likelihood frameworks, our results show that our methods improve consensus tree resolution in scenarios with low to moderate phylogenetic signal, while providing better or comparable dissimilarities to the true phylogeny. Applying our methods to mammals, Ebola virus, and a large HIV dataset of over nine thousand taxa confirms the improvement with real data. These results demonstrate the usefulness of our new consensus tree methods for analyzing the large datasets that are available today. Our software, PhyloCRISP, is available from https://github.com/yukiregista/PhyloCRISP.

title: Mapping evidence on factors contributing to delayed Ebola outbreak detection and response in Sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review
abstract: This protocol describes a scoping review that aims to map the available evidence on factors contributing to delays in Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak detection and public health response in sub-Saharan Africa. Guided by the Arksey and O’Malley framework, subsequent methodological refinements, and the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology, the review will follow the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) reporting guidance. It will examine delays across the outbreak detection and response continuum, including case recognition, healthcare presentation, suspected-case identification, diagnostic testing and laboratory confirmation, surveillance and outbreak recognition, and the initiation of public health response measures. It will also map individual, community, health system, institutional, logistical, political, security, environmental, and contextual determinants of these delays. Relevant peer-reviewed studies and eligible grey literature published from 1 January 1976 to the final search date will be considered, with searches covering English- and French-language sources. The findings will be synthesised descriptively and thematically to characterise the evidence base, identify knowledge gaps, and inform research, policy, and public health practice aimed at improving the timeliness of Ebola outbreak detection and response in sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Bundibugyo virus disease in outbreak settings: A practical clinical review
abstract: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) is a severe filovirus infection caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an orthoebolavirus with diagnostic and countermeasure implications distinct from Ebola virus (EBOV). The ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has expanded substantially, with 7890 confirmed cases and 3799 deaths reported across 63 health zones in seven provinces as of 23 September 2026. BVD usually presents as a nonspecific febrile and gastrointestinal illness; haemorrhagic manifestations are uncommon at presentation. Early outbreak investigation also showed that EBOV-oriented testing can fail to detect BDBV, making species-appropriate molecular testing essential when BDBV is epidemiologically plausible. Supportive care remains the standard of management, but what can be delivered safely differs between peripheral facilities and dedicated filovirus treatment centres. First-contact facilities should prioritise recognition, separation, protected sampling, treatment of immediately life-threatening or common treatable conditions, and early referral; treatment centres can provide closer monitoring, advanced supportive care, and access to approved research protocols. Insecurity, displacement, laboratory and transport constraints, and delayed presentation continue to limit implementation. No vaccine or specific therapeutic has established clinical efficacy against BDBV in humans; Ervebo is being evaluated within research protocols and the PARTNERS trial is evaluating MBP134 and remdesivir-based regimens. This review synthesises historical and current evidence on recognition, diagnosis, clinical care, infection prevention, referral, and emerging countermeasures in outbreak-affected settings.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), a severe filovirus infection caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an orthoebolavirus distinct from Ebola virus (EBOV). It highlights the clinical presentation of BVD as a nonspecific febrile and gastrointestinal illness, with rare haemorrhagic manifestations. The ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reported 7890 confirmed cases and 3799 deaths as of 23 September 2026. The review emphasizes the importance of species-appropriate molecular testing for BDBV, as EBOV-oriented tests may fail to detect it. It also outlines the limitations in outbreak management due to insecurity, displacement, and logistical challenges. Currently, no vaccine or specific therapeutic has established clinical efficacy against BDBV, with Ervebo and the PARTNERS trial evaluating potential treatments. The review underscores the need for tailored supportive care, with peripheral facilities focusing on immediate life-threatening conditions and early referral, while dedicated treatment centres provide advanced care and access to research protocols.

source_body_en: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) is a severe filovirus infection caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an orthoebolavirus with diagnostic and countermeasure implications distinct from Ebola virus (EBOV). The ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has expanded substantially, with 7890 confirmed cases and 3799 deaths reported across 63 health zones in seven provinces as of 23 September 2026. BVD usually presents as a nonspecific febrile and gastrointestinal illness; haemorrhagic manifestations are uncommon at presentation. Early outbreak investigation also showed that EBOV-oriented testing can fail to detect BDBV, making species-appropriate molecular testing essential when BDBV is epidemiologically plausible. Supportive care remains the standard of management, but what can be delivered safely differs between peripheral facilities and dedicated filovirus treatment centres. First-contact facilities should prioritise recognition, separation, protected sampling, treatment of immediately life-threatening or common treatable conditions, and early referral; treatment centres can provide closer monitoring, advanced supportive care, and access to approved research protocols. Insecurity, displacement, laboratory and transport constraints, and delayed presentation continue to limit implementation. No vaccine or specific therapeutic has established clinical efficacy against BDBV in humans; Ervebo is being evaluated within research protocols and the PARTNERS trial is evaluating MBP134 and remdesivir-based regimens. This review synthesises historical and current evidence on recognition, diagnosis, clinical care, infection prevention, referral, and emerging countermeasures in outbreak-affected settings.
